title: Document — the YAML frontmatter every Markdown file carries
_role: Every .md file in the repository validates against this, enforced by systems_check.py `check_document_frontmatter` ([D11]). There is no derived document register: the frontmatter IS the register, read by walking the tree, so there is nothing that can fall out of step with it.
_why: Filesystem dates carry NO information in this repository -- the history is a squashed import and every file reports the same date -- so freshness has to be declared and enforced rather than computed.
Roughly seventy of 189 markdown files were one-off session reports, indistinguishable from durable references by their path. `kind` + `status` is what tells them apart.

The repository already wrote all of this -- role banners, status lines, supersession markers, generated-file banners -- in four incompatible informal conventions, none machine-readable. This captures what was already being written.
_superseded_role: SUPERSEDED, RETAINED (2026-08-06). This field previously read: 'Every .md file in the repository validates against this. The register of all documents is systems/graph/documents.json, built by scanning frontmatter; the frontmatter is the source, the register is derived.' BOTH HALVES WERE FALSE and had been since the schema was written. `systems/graph/documents.json` never existed, and NO file validated against this schema -- it was loaded by SchemaSet, checked to be a well-formed schema, and then applied to nothing. What actually enforced frontmatter was a hardcoded key list inside check_documents that omitted `level` and `kind` entirely. So the contract had two homes and they had ALREADY DRIFTED in four measured ways: `_backfilled` (141 files), `superseded_in_part`, `history_only` and `frozen` -- the last two READ BY THE CHECKER ITSELF -- were absent here while `additionalProperties: false` would have rejected every one of them; `last_verified: unverified`, the deliberately-honest value 126 documents carry and which check_documents reports on by name, was forbidden by the date pattern; and CONVENTIONS.md's authoring template listed 10 of the 12 `kind` values, omitting `index`, which 9 live documents use. A schema that validates nothing cannot notice that it has gone wrong.

level.description: Which zoom level this document belongs to, or em-dash for documents outside the hierarchy (policy, runbook, licence).

kind.description: `prereg` implies status `immutable`. `generated` implies the file is rendered by a checker and hand-edits fail the build.

status.description: `immutable` is RESERVED for preregistrations: their entire value is that they were written before the result, so they are never rewritten, consolidated or tidied. Amendments are appended as dated blocks and the checker fails on any edit to the body.

canonical_for.description: The concepts this file OWNS. The load-bearing field: it is how a reader finds the owner of a fact, and how the checker detects two documents claiming the same concept. An empty array is valid and common -- most documents own nothing and point at owners.

scope.description: What it covers -- and, where it matters, what it deliberately does not.

supersedes.description: Paths or DOC- ids this replaces. Every entry must have a row in systems/MIGRATION.md -- nothing is superseded without a forwarding address.

superseded_by.description: REQUIRED when status is `superseded`. A superseded document with no successor is a dead end wearing a redirect.

last_verified.description: When someone last checked the content is STILL TRUE -- not when it was last edited. The distinction is the point: an edited-but-unverified document is exactly as stale as an untouched one. ⛔ `unverified` IS A LEGITIMATE VALUE AND NOT A HOLE: the bulk backfill read none of these documents, and stamping them with its own run date would have claimed a verification nobody performed, in the one field whose entire job is to say how stale something is. check_documents reports the count as [D5] and it is meant to fall. Forbidding it here -- which this schema did until 2026-08-06 -- would have forced exactly the dishonest stamp.

aliases.description: Other names this document has been cited under, so a reader who arrives with a stale name still lands here.

generator.description: REQUIRED when status is `generated`: the module that renders it.

owns_ids.description: Model object ids whose owner{file} points at this document. Derived; used to catch a document being archived while it still owns a fact.

superseded_in_part.description: A document that is PARTLY superseded is not `superseded` -- it is still live and still the owner of everything the successor did not take. Naming the successor here says which part moved without retiring the whole file.

history_only.description: READ BY check_documents [D8]. A `historical`/`superseded` document that something still DEPENDS on is normally a defect -- but a correction register has to stay reachable to do its job. This declares that the combination is deliberate.

frozen.description: READ BY check_documents [D10]. `false` marks a preregistration that is still a DRAFT, so it may not carry `immutable` -- the repository's strongest evidentiary claim is that a prereg was written before the result, and a draft wearing that status is the one thing that could erode it.

_backfilled.description: This frontmatter was written by systems/backfill_frontmatter.py from the document's own banner and path, NOT by someone who read the document. It is the honest provenance of `purpose` and `scope` on 141 files, and it travels with `last_verified: unverified`. Clear it when a human verifies the document.
